propositions: Batching N candidate digests into one call per ordering reduces call count from 2N to 2*ceil(N/batch_size), eliminating duplicate prefix transmission and cutting total input tokens by 48% on measured corpus.

Hoisting the shared query digest in the system prompt plus adding batch protocol instructions to that prompt grows the stable prefix from 873 to 1,337 tokens, crossing the 1024-token caching floor and enabling write-once-read-many behavior for subsequent calls.

Demultiplexing batched verdicts by candidate_id label rather than position ensures each candidate receives exactly one verdict; missing or unlabelled entries abstain only that candidate without affecting others.

Batching introduces systematic relation-label shifts on 6/12 ordered pairs (5 conservative, 1 ambiguous), with no loss of true-positive recall on synthetic positive control; shift is reproducible across runs and unrelated to sampling noise.
